## This is my second blog post.

# ============================================================
# 1. Load Packages
# ============================================================

library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)


# ============================================================
# 2. Read the Website
# ============================================================

# Main page of Books to Scrape
base_url <- "https://books.toscrape.com/"

page <- read_html(base_url)


# ============================================================
# 3. Get Book Categories and Their Links
# ============================================================

# Extract category names
category_names <- page %>%
  html_elements(".side_categories ul li ul li a") %>%
  html_text2()

# Extract category links
category_links <- page %>%
  html_elements(".side_categories ul li ul li a") %>%
  html_attr("href")

# Combine category names and links into a data frame
categories <- data.frame(
  category = category_names,
  link = category_links
)

# Check the category data
head(categories)
nrow(categories)


# ============================================================
# 4. Create a Function to Scrape Each Category
# ============================================================

scrape_category <- function(category_name, category_link) {
  
  # Create the URL for the first page of the category
  current_url <- paste0(
    base_url,
    category_link
  )
  
  # Create an empty data frame to store results
  all_books <- data.frame()
  
  repeat {
    
    # Read the current page
    category_page <- read_html(current_url)
    
    # Find all books on the current page
    books <- category_page %>%
      html_elements(".product_pod")
    
    # Extract book information
    page_data <- data.frame(
      
      title = books %>%
        html_element("h3 a") %>%
        html_attr("title"),
      
      price = books %>%
        html_element(".price_color") %>%
        html_text2(),
      
      rating = books %>%
        html_element(".star-rating") %>%
        html_attr("class"),
      
      category = category_name
    )
    
    # Add the current page to the accumulated results
    all_books <- bind_rows(
      all_books,
      page_data
    )
    
    # Look for a link to the next page
    next_link <- category_page %>%
      html_element("li.next a") %>%
      html_attr("href")
    
    # Stop if there is no next page
    if (is.na(next_link)) {
      break
    }
    
    # Convert the relative next-page link to an absolute URL
    current_url <- url_absolute(
      next_link,
      current_url
    )
    
    # Pause briefly between requests
    Sys.sleep(0.5)
  }
  
  return(all_books)
}


# ============================================================
# 5. Scrape All Categories
# ============================================================

# Create an empty data frame for all books
books_all <- data.frame()

for (i in 1:nrow(categories)) {
  
  # Scrape one category
  category_data <- scrape_category(
    categories$category[i],
    categories$link[i]
  )
  
  # Add it to the complete dataset
  books_all <- bind_rows(
    books_all,
    category_data
  )
  
  # Display progress
  print(
    paste(
      "Finished:",
      categories$category[i]
    )
  )
  
  # Pause briefly between categories
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
}


# ============================================================
# 6. Check the Scraped Data
# ============================================================

# Number of books collected
nrow(books_all)

# Preview the data
head(books_all)

# Number of books in each category
table(books_all$category)

# Check for duplicated titles
sum(duplicated(books_all$title))


# ============================================================
# 7. Clean the Data
# ============================================================

books_clean <- books_all %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Convert price from text such as "£45.17" to 45.17
    price = parse_number(price),
    
    # Convert star ratings from text to numbers
    rating = case_when(
      rating == "star-rating One" ~ 1,
      rating == "star-rating Two" ~ 2,
      rating == "star-rating Three" ~ 3,
      rating == "star-rating Four" ~ 4,
      rating == "star-rating Five" ~ 5,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 8. Check the Cleaned Data
# ============================================================

# Preview cleaned data
head(books_clean)

# Check variable types
str(books_clean)

# Check for missing values
colSums(is.na(books_clean))

# Summary statistics
summary(books_clean)


# ============================================================
# 9. Summarize Books by Category
# ============================================================

category_summary <- books_clean %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(
    number_of_books = n(),
    average_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    average_rating = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ============================================================
# 10. Explore Category-Level Results
# ============================================================

# Categories with the lowest average prices
lowest_price_categories <- category_summary %>%
  arrange(average_price) %>%
  select(
    category,
    number_of_books,
    average_price,
    median_price,
    average_rating
  ) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

lowest_price_categories


# Categories with the highest average ratings
highest_rating_categories <- category_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(average_rating)) %>%
  select(
    category,
    number_of_books,
    average_price,
    median_price,
    average_rating
  ) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

highest_rating_categories

################################Analysis
reliable_categories <- category_summary %>%
  filter(number_of_books >= 10)
reliable_categories

overall_avg_price <- mean(books_clean$price, na.rm = TRUE)
overall_avg_rating <- mean(books_clean$rating, na.rm = TRUE)
overall_avg_price
overall_avg_rating

best_value_categories <- reliable_categories %>%
  filter(
    average_price < overall_avg_price,
    average_rating > overall_avg_rating
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(average_rating))

best_value_categories


nrow(reliable_categories)
overall_avg_price
overall_avg_rating
best_value_categories
